findings.title: kickReserveAuction can be called while liquidation auctions with bad debt are still unsettled
findings.evidence: `kickReserveAuction()` has no guard that liquidation auctions are cleared before kicking the claimable-reserve auction (rc6 contains neither the older `_revertIfAuctionClearable(auctions, loans)` nor the fix's `_revertIfActiveAuctions(auctions)`; the only checks are the 2-week/72-hour timers). Any external caller can therefore kick a reserve auction (`KickerActions.kickReserveAuction`, Pool.sol:421) while a liquidation auction whose borrower still carries bad debt is pending. `KickerActions.kickReserveAuction` derives the claimable amount from the pool's full `t0PoolDebt * inflator` (see `_claimableReserves`, PoolHelper.sol:299-324), including debt that will never be repaid, moves it into `reserveAuction_.unclaimed` and pays msg.sender a 1% kicker award. Because `SettlerActions.settlePoolDebt` (SettlerActions.sol:135-146) settles a borrower's bad debt from pool reserves computed as `assets - liabilities`, and `liabilities` includes `reserveAuction_.unclaimed`, kicking the reserve auction first removes the reserves that would have absorbed the bad debt; the un-covered debt is then written off against the HPB bucket via `_forgiveBadDebt` (SettlerActions.sol:443-500), transferring the loss to HPB/lender deposits. Upstream fixed exactly this by adding `_revertIfActiveAuctions` (commit e258a849, "Liquidation of positions with bad debt can cause losses for HPB depositors").

findings.title: Anyone can settle a borrower's bad debt out of pool reserves with no cap, allowing reserves to be drained
findings.evidence: In `settlePoolDebt`, once the borrower has no collateral left (`borrower.collateral == 0`) the remaining `borrower.t0Debt` is reduced directly by `Maths.min(borrower.t0Debt, Maths.floorWdiv(assets - liabilities, poolState_.inflator))`, i.e. pool reserves are used to repay the debt. There is no cap (no time gate, no per-borrower reserve limit) and `settle()` is permissionless (`ERC20Pool.settle`, ERC20Pool.sol:363). An attacker controlling a lender account and a borrower account can manufacture bad debt: deposit in a bucket far above market to inflate LUP, pull almost all collateral from the loan (BorrowerActions removeCollateral path), lender-kick the borrower to revive HTP, `bucketTake` until the collateral is consumed so only a small residual debt remains, then call `settle()` to have that residual debt paid from reserves; the attacker then withdraws the LP, extracting the reserves, and repeats. Reachable and unbounded in this snapshot; upstream removed reserve-funded bad debt settlement (commits 290d6cf6 / ce7b42b4, fix for Sherlock-3 "Reserves can be stolen by settling artificially created bad debt from them").

findings.title: Bucket-bankruptcy check in _forgiveBadDebt uses unscaled deposit value
findings.evidence: `_forgiveBadDebt` tracks `depositRemaining` in unscaled (Fenwick) units (it is `unscaledDeposit - Maths.wdiv(debt, scale)`), but the bankruptcy check multiplies it by `Maths.WAD` instead of the bucket's `scale`: `if (depositRemaining * Maths.WAD + hpbBucket.collateral * _priceAt(index) <= bucketLP)`. When a bucket's scale differs from 1e18 the exchange-rate-rounds-to-zero test is off by the scale factor, so a healthy bucket can be declared bankrupt and `hpbBucket.lps` set to 0 (forfeiting all depositors' LP) or a genuinely dust bucket can be missed. The branch is reachable by anyone calling `settle()` on a kicked borrower that still has bad debt (requires `borrower.t0Debt != 0 && borrower.collateral == 0` after step 1) in a pool where the HPB deposit carrying the write-off has a non-1e18 scale. Upstream fixed this by scaling `depositRemaining` (commits 34734cbc / 03d255d7, "HPB may be incorrectly bankrupt due to use of unscaled value in _forgiveBadDebt").
